correctness.rationale: The generalized-quadrangle incidence axioms yield all ten side-and-distance ordered pair types. All 84 listed third-vertex extension cells have exact nonnegative counts given by closed formulas; for \(s,t\ge2\) every listed count is strictly positive and all omitted cells are impossible. Duality covers the other five types. The preserved side and exact distance of up to two stationary pebbles supplies a matching third vertex indefinitely, so the \(\mathrm{FO}^3\) equivalence is not an extrapolation from finite examples. Four point-vertices pairwise at distance 2 exist exactly when a line has at least four points (s>=3), proving a width-four separation in the named-distance signature; minimum graph size is 30 by the parameter formula. The bundled standard-library verifier reproduces the exact count table on 30-, 80-, and 72-vertex classical examples; 3600 parameter checks corroborate positivity and both side totals. The full algebraic derivation appears in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: Qualified originality assessment: relevant geometry sources treat generalized-quadrangle parameters, automorphism classifications, and individual fixed-order uniqueness, not an all-parameter unrestricted-depth \(\mathrm{FO}^3\) theorem in the full distance-enriched signature in the inspected material. General support-based finite-variable reasoning is relevant but its distance-regular specialization does not cover nonregular incidence graphs with \(s\ne t\), while symmetric 2-design incidence graphs have a different diameter-three incidence geometry. Published semantic searches did not expose a theorem with equivalent or dominating hypotheses. This is not an exhaustive priority proof; see residual risks.
residual_risks: A general theorem about coherent configurations, relation algebras, or finite-variable equivalence may imply the presented explicit quadrangle case even without naming it.

value.rationale: The theorem completely identifies a single unbounded-quantifier-depth \(\mathrm{FO}^3\) theory throughout a canonical class of finite thick generalized quadrangles, including geometries whose incidence graphs have unequal degrees. Naming exact distances does not break the collapse, while a natural four-point collinearity property distinguishes examples with four variables, giving a sharp logical-variable boundary. It additionally provides the sharp 30-vertex smallest representative. The result is a structural field/parameter-blindness phenomenon for foundational incidence geometries rather than a routine finite-table recomputation.
